answer:
Neil Armstrong served in the **Korean War** as a U.S. Navy fighter pilot. He flew 78 combat missions during this conflict.

The Korean War effectively ended when the **Armistice Agreement was signed on July 27, 1953**, in Panmunjom. While the fighting ceased on that date and Neil Armstrong had completed his final combat mission earlier on March 5, 1952, the war officially concluded three years later with the armistice. It's worth noting that while there was an armistice (cease-fire), no formal peace treaty has ever been signed between North and South Korea, so technically the Korean peninsula remains in a state of technical war, though the active combat phase definitely ended on July 27, 1953.
